title: Miami Beach Ocean Watersports

services.name: Parasailing
services.desc: The bay view nobody gets from the sand - a short ride off the Beach and you're airborne over Biscayne Bay. You can see the water from your balcony on Miami Beach. This is how you get above it. The trip runs about an hour on the boat, of which five to ten minutes are spent hanging under the canopy at up to four hundred feet, with Key Biscayne on one side and the downtown skyline on the other. You leave from Pier 9 at Dinner Key Marina - a fifteen-minute drive from South Beach - because the bay there sits behind the barrier islands and stays flyable on afternoons when the ocean side is too churned up to launch. services.name: Banana Boat
services.desc: Everyone straddles an inflatable, the boat takes up the slack, and the only real question is how long the group stays on before somebody goes sideways and takes the rest with them. Thirty minutes, from age five, priced per rider - which is why it's the standard move for families and for groups who want one thing everybody can do together regardless of how brave they are. Falling off is not the failure state, it's the entire point. We run it in the protected water off Dinner Key, so the surface is smooth enough for it to be funny rather than jarring. services.name: Boat Tour
services.desc: Not everyone crosses the causeway wanting adrenaline. This is a thirty-minute guided run out of Dinner Key at a pace that lets you look around, take photographs that aren't blurred, and hear what you're looking at. The captain covers the marina, the shoreline and whatever the bay decides to show you - manatees and dolphins are common enough that regulars stop being surprised. No age minimum, no swimming, no equipment. It's the one grandparents, toddlers and everyone in between can do on the same boat, and it works well as the opening act for a group where half the party is booked on something faster afterwards. services.name: Jet Ski
services.desc: An hour on your own ski across protected water, a quarter-hour from South Beach. An hour, dock to dock, on your own machine. You idle out of the marina through the no-wake channel, and once the guide clears the zone the bay is yours to use. The reason riders come over from the Beach is the surface: this side of Key Biscayne is protected, so instead of slamming through ocean chop you get long, flat stretches where the throttle is actually usable. One or two riders per ski, and the two-up costs less than booking a pair of singles. Drivers need to be eighteen; sixteen and seventeen year olds can drive with a legal guardian riding the same ski. services.name: Flyboard
services.desc: The one your friends on the Beach will not believe you did - and yes, first-timers get up. A board plumbed to a jet ski fires water under your feet hard enough to lift you clear of the bay. It looks impossible from the dock and it is genuinely learnable in about ten minutes: the instructor controls the throttle from the water beside you and feeds you power as your balance catches up, so almost everyone is standing well inside the session. You get twenty minutes on the board, from age eight up. We run it in the sheltered water off Dinner Key rather than out on the ocean side, which matters more here than for anything else we do - flat water is what makes the first climb out feel steady
